Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Nexus Security Solutions Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Nexus Security Solutions' results for the third quarter of 2024. With me on today's call are David Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Kline, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Lisa Wong, Chief Security Officer; Tom Hargrove, VP of Sales; and Rachel Lee, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Chen.

David Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report another strong quarter for Nexus Security Solutions. Our results reflect the growing importance of cybersecurity in today's digital landscape and our ability to deliver innovative solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. The market reception to Nexus Guardian has been overwhelmingly positive, significantly contributing to its rapid adoption and outsized revenue impact across our endpoint detection and response, secure access service edge, and extended detection and response platforms.

Our strategy is built on seven key pillars: executing on our full-year revenue and profitability outlook, driving marketing spend efficiency, enhancing the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, navigating the impact of currency fluctuations on revenue, staying ahead of the evolving threat landscape, expanding the number of customers with ARR over $100K, and accelerating the number of new customers acquired.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Kline to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, David. We achieved record revenue of $350 million in the third quarter, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained healthy at 82%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $265 million. Net income was $65 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.51. We are raising our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

As David outlined earlier, we've delivered another quarter of strong execution against our strategic priorities in endpoint detection and response (EDR), secure access service edge (SASE), and extended detection and response (XDR) platforms. Today, I'll dive into our full-year outlook for revenue and profitability, incorporating the momentum from our Q3 results and the robust pipeline visibility we have entering Q4.

First, on full-year revenue guidance. We're raising our FY24 revenue outlook to a range of $1.38 billion to $1.42 billion, representing approximately 26% to 30% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This is an increase from our prior guide of $1.32 billion to $1.36 billion and reflects better-than-expected consumption in our Nexus XDR platform, accelerated adoption of our AI-powered Nexus Guardian behavioral analytics engine, and outsized wins in our cloud-native SASE offerings.

To give you a sense of the breakdown: Subscription revenue, which now comprises 92% of total revenue, is expected to grow 31% to 33% YoY to $1.27 billion to $1.30 billion. This is fueled by net retention rates holding steady at 118%—our highest in three years—driven by upsell opportunities in zero-trust network access (ZTNA) and cloud workload protection (CWP). Large enterprises, particularly in financial services and healthcare, are expanding footprints post-initial deployments, with average annual contract values (ACVs) for our top 50 customers up 15% to over $2.5 million. Professional services and other revenue will contribute the balance, growing 8% to 10% as we scale our managed detection and response (MDR) services, now serving over 1,200 clients through our global SOC network. By product line: Nexus XDR is pacing for 35% growth, outpacing the broader EDR market as estimated by IDC at 22% CAGR through 2027. Our SASE portfolio, bolstered by the integration of last year's acquisition of EdgeFortress, is tracking to 42% growth, capitalizing on the SASE market's projected $15 billion TAM by 2026 per Gartner. Legacy network security solutions, while maturing at 12% growth, remain a stable high-margin base.

Regionally, we're seeing balanced strength: Americas (65% of revenue): 28% growth, propelled by ransomware surges—think the Change Healthcare breach earlier this year—and regulatory tailwinds from CMMC 2.0 compliance in defense. We've landed 15 deals with Fortune 500 firms averaging $10 million+ TCV. EMEA (20% of revenue): 32% growth, accelerating on NIS2 Directive mandates and GDPR enforcement. UK and German public sector wins, including a €50 million multi-year contract with a major telco, underscore our edge in sovereign cloud integrations with Azure and OVHcloud. APAC (15% of revenue): 25% growth, with China and India driving upside via PDPA and DPDP Act compliance. Partnerships with Alibaba Cloud and Tencent have unlocked hyperscale opportunities, offsetting softer Japan enterprise spending.

Key trends underpinning this outlook include the exponential rise in AI-augmented threats—up 65% YoY per our threat intelligence reports, mirroring CrowdStrike's Falcon OverWatch data—and the shift to consolidated platforms amid platform fatigue. Our technical initiatives, like rolling out Nexus Guardian 2.0 with generative AI for autonomous threat hunting (reducing MTTR by 40% in beta tests), position us to capture share from point solutions like legacy Symantec Endpoint or Check Point gateways.

Now, turning to profitability. We're guiding to adjusted non-GAAP operating margins of 22% to 24% for FY24, expanding 250 basis points from last year and ahead of our prior 20-22% range. This reflects: Gross margins stable at 82% to 83%, with subscription mix benefits offsetting a modest 2% headwind from AWS co-sell investments. OpEx discipline: Sales and marketing at 38% of revenue (down from 41% last year) as we optimize our channel ecosystem—now 55% of bookings via partners like Deloitte and WWT—while R&D holds at 14% to fuel innovations like our OT/IoT security module, targeting the $10 billion ICS/OT market underserved by Palo Alto's Prisma and Fortinet's FortiGate. Adjusted EBITDA of $315 million to $340 million, or 23% margins, with free cash flow conversion exceeding 110% of EBITDA.

Non-GAAP EPS is now projected at $2.45 to $2.55, assuming 128 million diluted shares, up from $2.15 to $2.25 prior. This embeds about $25 million in stock-based comp and excludes $18 million in amortization from acquisitions.

Strategically, we're prioritizing platform consolidation and AI differentiation to sustain 25%+ organic growth into FY25. Risks to this outlook include elongated sales cycles in a high-interest-rate environment (currently averaging 9 months for seven-figure deals) and potential U.S.-China trade tensions impacting APAC supply chains. However, our $850 million cash position, zero net debt, and 95% dollar-based net retention provide ample buffer. We've also authorized an additional $200 million share repurchase, signaling confidence.

In summary, FY24 shapes up as a breakout year, validating our 'Unified Threat Intelligence' vision amid a cybersecurity spending boom—Gartner forecasts 13.5% global growth to $212 billion. We're well-positioned to outperform, much like peers Zscaler and SentinelOne have in recent quarters.

Before I hand over, a quick note on currency fluctuations, which have been top of mind. As a global leader with 52% of revenue from outside the Americas, the strong U.S. dollar created headwinds. On a reported basis, Q3 revenue grew 28% YoY, but constant currency would show 32%, with FX shaving about $14 million or 4.5 points off growth. EMEA took the biggest hit from euro and pound weakness, masking 35% local currency ARR growth; APAC from yen depreciation despite 42% constant currency expansion; LATAM milder from BRL moves. We've hedged 70% of exposures, ramped local invoicing to 45%, and expect 3-4% FY headwind. Our constant currency guide of $1.38-1.42 billion reflects organic strength.

Now, over to Mike Patel for our technology update.

Mike Patel: Thank you, Sarah. Our technology roadmap is focused on delivering next-generation security solutions that leverage artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas of focus include staying ahead of the evolving threat landscape.

Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining us on the Q3 earnings call. Before diving deeper, I want to provide our quarterly commentary on the threat landscape—a critical factor driving our growth and demand. The threat environment in 2024 has entered a polycrisis era, with cybercriminals, nation-states, and hacktivists using generative AI, quantum challenges, and open-source tools at scale. Our Nexus Threat Intelligence Lab, aggregating data from 2.5 billion endpoints daily, saw a 37% YoY increase in high-severity incidents in Q3, aligning with MITRE ATT&CK and reports from CrowdStrike and Mandiant noting over 1,200 ransomware variants last quarter.

Ransomware dominates at 42% of engagements, up 15% sequentially, evolving to RaaS with groups like LockBit 3.0 achieving 72-hour dwell times and double-extortion in 68% of cases, per Mandiant's M-Trends. Our FalconXDR blocked 1.2 million payloads, up 52% YoY, via behavioral AI.

AI-powered attacks surged: phishing with LLMs up 45%, deepfake vishing 210% in finance, polymorphic malware 30%. Our GenAI Shield detects 96% of synthetics. Supply chain risks at 22% of breaches, up from 14%, with 450+ mitigations tied to vendors like Ivanti; our SBOM integration cuts MTTI by 40%.

Cloud/identity threats up 61%, with 18,000 service account detections from Cozy Bear. Zero Trust Edge blocks 89% lateral movement.

Regionally: North America (52% ARR) faces SEC rules, DoD CMMC, China APTs; federal up 35%. EMEA (28%) NIS2, GDPR fines €2.8B; manufacturing ransomware. APAC (15%) mobile malware 55%, Lazarus crypto thefts. LATAM eCrime up 30%.

We're investing 22% of revenue, $185M in FY24, in AI/ML (99.2% true positives), quantum crypto (Kyber/Dilithium), autonomous SOC (75% Level 1 automation, MTTR <5 min), and integrations with Prisma, Okta, ServiceNow. Gartner sees EDR/XDR at $12.5B by 2027, 18% CAGR; our 125% NRR confirms stickiness.

Thank you. Now to Lisa for security posture.

Lisa Wong: We are committed to providing our customers with the highest level of security. We are constantly monitoring the threat landscape and adapting our security posture to protect against emerging threats, from AI-augmented ransomware to supply chain compromises, ensuring our platforms deliver resilience across multi-cloud and zero-trust environments.

Tom Hargrove: Thank you, Lisa. We are seeing strong demand for our solutions across all geographies and industry verticals. Our sales team is focused on building strong relationships with our customers and partners, which has proven highly effective in our go-to-market strategy.

Today, I'd like to highlight the effectiveness of our GTM, a cornerstone of our record Q3 results. In cybersecurity, where threats evolve rapidly, our partner-led, product-led growth hybrid delivered 42% YoY ARR growth to $1.28 billion, NRR to 128% from 118%, amid 65% ransomware surge per Chainalysis.

Channel partnerships drove 62% of new ACV at $4.2M record; integrations with AWS, Azure boost MDR attach 35%; Microsoft co-sell $150M pipeline; Velocity Program cuts CAC payback to 9 months.

Direct sales: 28% large deal growth >$1M ACV, 68% POV conversion via GenAI demos (MTTD -87%). PLG freemium EDR 45K downloads, 18% paid conversion.

Regions: Americas 55% ARR, 51% growth on CISA zero-trust, six agency deals. EMEA 62% to 25%, NIS2, DACH SASE 40%. APAC 89% to 20%, sovereign cloud vs. Lazarus.

Quantum-Resistant add-on +15% upsell; outcome pricing churn 4.2%; inbound 2.5x MQLs. Headwinds: macro cycles +15%, but 3.2x LTV:CAC. Guide 40-45% ARR FY24, Q4 channels 65%, APAC 25%; battle-tested for $75B TAM, 14% CAGR.

Separately, on customer metrics: Q3 ended with 458 customers over $100K ARR, up 37% YoY from 334, 14% sequential from 402. They contribute 68% total ARR, NRR 118%, driven by CyberShield Nexus unifying SIEMs (70% new wins), ZTA cert post-Okta.

North America 72% (330, +32%), AWS/Azure embeds. EMEA 52% (78, +52%), GDPR DACH OEM. APAC 48% (50), sovereign vs. Volt Typhoon. Fortune 1000: 187 (41%), +42 logos; churn <2%, ARR/customer $248K +11%. Year-end >550, $2.1B pipeline.

And new customers: Acquired 1,247 new logos, 42% YoY from 878, total 18,500 (+28%). Net new ARR $142M, quarterly ARR +36%, outpacing IDC 15-18%.

Enterprise 156 (+68%), Fortune 50 finance/healthcare displacing Splunk/Cortex. Mid-market 742 (+39%), cloud ZTNA, channels 62%. SMB 349 (+28%), freemium 22%.

Regions: NA 68% (849, +45%), SEC rules. EMEA 22% (274, +52%), NIS2. APAC 10% (124, +35%), Tokyo DC.

Initiatives: Nexus AI Guardian 31% POC-paid; 4,200 partners 58% logos; 27% XDR share post-CrowdStrike. Q3 guide 1,300-1,400, NRR 128%.

Rachel Lee: Thank you, Tom. Our marketing efforts are focused on building brand awareness and generating demand for our solutions. We are using a variety of channels to reach our target audience, including digital marketing, public relations, and events, with a sharp eye on spend efficiency.

This quarter, marketing spend efficiency stood out as a profitability driver. In Q3, we deployed $28.2 million, 14.2% of revenue—flat YoY despite 28% topline to $350 million—sixth straight sub-15% quarter, below Gartner 18-20% median. CAC improved 18% to $4,750/ARR customer, payback 11 months from 14 (peers 16-18). ROAS 6.2x from 4.8x, MQL-SQL 28% (+35%), LTV:CAC 4.8:1.

Initiatives: ABM for top 2,000 accounts via 6sense/Demandbase (42% pipeline, 7.5x ROAS, $450K avg). ThreatLens content 52% inbound ($1,200 CAC), deepfake reports 3x engagement. Digital: CPC -22% to $18.50 on 'Falcon alternatives'; video MITRE demos. Events: RSA $15M pipeline 9x; AWS/Azure co-marketing 25% logos.

Regions: NA 72% spend, CAC $4,200 7.1x. EMEA 18%, 5.8x NIS2. APAC 10%, 42% lift PDPA/DPDP.

Future: $10M GenAI nurture, Q4 $29-31M (13-14%), CAC <$4,500 ROAS >6.5x; outpace peers as multi-cloud/quantum accelerate 25% growth per IDC.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press star then 1 on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. We'll pause momentarily to assemble the queue. First question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Sarah, can you expand on the full-year outlook risks, especially macro and FX? And how does currency impact bookings?

Sarah Kline: Thanks, John. On risks, high rates elongate cycles to 9 months for big deals, and U.S.-China tensions could hit APAC chains, but $850M cash, no debt, 95% net retention buffer us. FX: 3-4% FY headwind baked in, hedges cover 70%, local invoicing 45%; focuses on USD federal growth mitigate. Bookings constant currency strong.

Operator: Next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen: Great results. Tom, thoughts on new customer adds sustainability amid competition? Any color on displacements?

Tom Hargrove: Emily, sustainability strong: 1,247 adds reflect Nexus AI Guardian 31% conversions, channels 58%, 27% XDR share. Displacements from Splunk, Cortex, Falcon post-outage—our 99.999% SLA key. Q4 1,300-1,400 guide with Nexus 6.0 beta.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Mike, impressive threat intel. How does this inform R&D allocation, and quantum readiness timeline?

Mike Patel: Raj, polycrisis—AI phishing 45%, supply chain 22%, identity 61%—drives 22% revenue R&D: AI Neural Engine 99.2% TPs, Kyber/Dilithium now in VPNs pre-NIST, AutoTriage 75% alerts. Quantum full rollout FY25, already +15% upsell velocity.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Grant with Barclays.

Lisa Grant: Rachel, marketing efficiency metrics—how sustainable with cookie changes? And tie to $100K cohort growth.

Rachel Lee: Lisa, sustainable via zero-party data, GenAI chatbots +15% SQL velocity. ABM/content ROAS 7.5x/3x fuel cohort: 458 $100K+ (68% ARR), Fortune 1000 +42 logos, expansions via Nexus Shield. Q4 CAC sub-$4,500 holds.

David Chen: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident in our ability to deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
